MINUTES
  Regular Meeting
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  Council Chambers, 111 South First Street
  September 23, 2024
  6:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL: At 6:07 p.m., on Monday, September 23, 2024, the Alhambra City Council met in
Council Chambers of the Alhambra City Hall.

PRESENT:  LEE, MALONEY, ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, PÉREZ
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, Deputy City Manager Hembree, City Attorney Montes,
City Clerk Myles, Director of Parks and Recreation Macias, Director of Library Services LohGuan,
Chief of Police Kennedy, Chief of Fire Department Ragusa, Director of Finance Lieu, Director of
Human Resources Ko, Director of Community Development Ho, Director of Public Works and Utilities
Ahlen, Battalion Chief Brown, Assistant Chief of Police Fuentes

FLAG SALUTE:  Led by Vice Mayor Lee

LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: We acknowledge that the land on which we are gathered is the
traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Gabrielino/Tongva peoples. We seek to prioritize
respect for the historic culture and contemporary presence of the native peoples throughout California,
especially in the greater Los Angeles/Alhambra area. We come with respect and gratitude for the
Gabrielino/Tongva people who still consider themselves the caretakers of this land. It is through their
examples that we are reminded of our greater responsibility to take care of Mother Earth and to take
care of each other.

PUBLIC HEARING

1.  EDWARD BYRNE MEMORIAL JUSTICE ASSISTANCE GRANT (JAG) – F2M5-41,
N2M24-85, M2M24-168

  This was the time and place set by Notice No. N2M24-85 for the City Council to hold a public
  hearing to receive community input concerning the use of funds received under the United
  States Department of Justice, Bureau of Justice Assistance Edward Byrne Memorial Justice
  Assistance Grant (JAG) Program. The 2024 JAG funds will be used to outfit a sergeant vehicle
  with modernized police technology to be utilized in emergent situations. The grant guidelines
  required the City conduct a public hearing to receive community input concerning the use of
  funds, and approval of the application and pertinent requirements. Once the City Council
  designated the Chief of Police as the JAG Grant Administrator, the Chief of Police, or his
  designee, was responsible for the distribution of funds, monitoring the award and submitting
  the required reports.

  Opened & Closed the Public Hearing: Mayor PÉREZ opened the public hearing and as
  there was no one present who wished to speak, closed the same.

  Discussion:  Vice Mayor LEE supported the grant.

  Action Taken:  After receiving public testimony, the Mayor closed the public hearing
  and the Council adopted Minute Order No. M2M24-168 as follows:

  RESOLVED by the Alhambra City Council that this Council hereby authorizes
  the City Manager, or her designee, to apply for United States Department of
  1
9-23-24
   Justice, Bureau of Justice Assistance -- Edward Byrne Memorial Justice
  Assistance Grant (JAG) Program funds in the amount of $11,284.00 and
  appropriates funds in the amount of $11,284.00 in FY 2024-25 upon grant
  award; and,

  BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED by the Alhambra City Council that this Council
  hereby ratifies the action of the City Manager in designating the Chief of Police
  or Designee as the administrator for said Grant.

  Vote:  Moved:  MAZA  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  LEE, MAZA, MALONEY, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

PRESENTATIONS

2.  EARTHQUAKE SAFETY AND ALHAMBRA EMERGENCY OPERATIONS AFTER AN
  EARTHQUAKE – F2M24-16

  At their August 26, 2024 meeting, Council requested an informational presentation regarding
  earthquake safety and preparedness. Battalion Chief BROWN presented information
  regarding the City’s actions/response as well as community expectations after an earthquake.
  The presentation is on file in the City Clerk’s office. Director of Human Resources/Risk
  Manager KO, City Manager BINNQUIST, and Battalion Chief BROWN also presented
  information regarding the City’s Community Emergency Response Team (CERT) Program
  and upcoming Safety Fair.

  Discussion: Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER stressed the importance of sharing the
  City’s plans and discussed age requirements for the CERT Program and programs targeted
  to teens with Battalion Chief Brown. Councilmembers MALONEY and MAZA thanked staff for
  the presentation and making the information available to the public.

  Vice Mayor LEE further discussed the plan with Battalion Chief BROWN with regards to
  emergency shelters for the public, methods for citywide announcements during an emergency,
  the public’s ability to address emergency situations as well as their ability to seek emergency
  services, the specific responsibilities of Council in an emergency, and the role of CERT
  certified members of the public. Ms. LEE requested a separate training session for
  Councilmembers.

  Mayor PÉREZ thanked staff for their presentation and supported Ms. Lee’s suggestion for a
  training session for Councilmembers. She requested additional information regarding
  earthquake safety building requirements and City Manager BINNQUIST stated that staff could
  provide that information in Council’s weekly newsletter.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and ordered filed this informational report.

3.  HOME OCCUPATION PERMITS – F2M24-16

  Director of Community Development HO delivered a staff report. At the June 24, 2024 meeting
  the City Council requested information regarding home occupation permits to discuss whether
  or not changes were needed to the existing code. Mr. HO presented information regarding
  home occupation permit forms; current regulations; types of home occupations currently
  allowed; mobile business licenses; and, cottage food operations/home kitchens. At this time,
  2
9-23-24
   following a review of the newly adopted codes, and considering neighborhood impacts, staff
  did not recommend any changes to home occupation regulations.

  Discussion: Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER supported staff’s work. Vice Mayor
  LEE and Mr. HO discussed home occupation permits with regards to automotive repair
  services, actions taken that would necessitate a permit, and additional types of services
  offered in homes.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and ordered filed this informational report.

CONSENT AGENDA (Item Nos. 4 – 26)

All items listed under the Consent Agenda, with the exception of Item No. 4 and 17, were considered
by the City Council to be routine and were enacted by one motion.

LEE: Vice Mayor Lee recused herself from the discussion of Item No. 4 as a homeowner in Alhambra
and to avoid any future conflict of interest. Ms. LEE left Council Chambers at 6:54 p.m.

4.  FIRST READING OF AN ORDINANCE ADDING CHAPTER 5.92 TO THE ALHAMBRA
  MUNICIPAL CODE TO ESTABLISH REGULATIONS FOR SHORT-TERM RENTALS –
F2M18-35, F2M24-33, O2M24-4836

  On August 26, 2024, the City Council considered an amendment to the Alhambra Municipal
  Code to include new regulations for short-term rentals (STRs). Following the presentation
  and public comment, the Council provided additional direction to add the following additional
  regulations: 1) Host: Host will be defined as a natural person or persons who are the owner of
  record on a property as illustrated on a deed or legal document. 2) Eligibility: Types of
  dwelling units that are eligible to be used as short-term rentals are single family residences,
  duplexes, condominiums, townhomes and multi-family rental units in buildings of less than 5
  units total. 3) Building Inspection Report: Inspections for all units were not feasible because of
  the amount of time needed. In lieu of an inspection, a building inspection report will be required
  to be submitted to the City annually to self-certify that the unit complies with regulations. Staff
  will be available to conduct inspections on a case-by-case basis. 4) Cap on STR Permits: A
  maximum number of short-term permits will be capped at 500. 5) Occupancy Limits: The
  maximum number of occupants for a short-term rental remain as originally proposed because
  an occupancy limit would be unfeasible on properties with more than three bedrooms. The
  current occupancy limits provide consistency and avoids disruption to existing STR operations.
  6) Grace Period to Obtain Permits: The grace period to obtain a short-term rental permit will
  begin March 1st. Anticipating, the Ordinance is adopted and goes into effect January 1st,
  outreach efforts will be conducted to ensure that all potential applicants are informed about
  the process and requirements for obtaining the necessary STR permit. The STR permit will be
  set to renew annually from the date that the permit was issued. 7) Appeal Process: An appeal
  process for a short-term rental revocation will be heard by the Planning Commission.
  Essentially, if a Host receives 3 violations in a 12-month period, their permit will be revoked.
  The operator can appeal that revocation to the Planning Commission.

  Public Comment:

  The following people spoke against the ordinance:
  1) Reagan Canaday, 1700 Grand View Dr.
  2) Richard Wong, 2517 Whitney Dr.
  3) Ryuu Yu, 512 N. Stoneman Ave.
  4) David Fu, 303 E. Valley Blvd #C
  5) Stephen Kung, 824 S. Olive Ave.
  3
9-23-24
   6) Brandon Tan, 303 E. Valley Blvd.
  7) Terry Quan, 303 E. Valley Blvd.
  8) Ning Li and his wife, 310 S. Moore Ave., Monterey Park, spoke via Mandarin translation
  provided by the Language Line
  9) Ki Fung Ma, 1459 Meekar Ave., La Puente, spoke via Cantonese translation provided by
  the Language Line
  10) Eric Ma, via Zoom
  11) Cordelia Colbert, via Zoom
  12) George, via Zoom

  The following people spoke in favor of the ordinance:
  1) Shirley Tatsuno, 1408 S. Fifth St. also stated that she believed all short-term rentals should
  be banned.
  2) Barbara Messina, via Zoom
  3) John Bwarie, via Zoom, representing the Alhambra Chamber of Commerce, supported
  regulations but suggested making additional changes to the ordinance before final
  approval such as the cap on units for multifamily complexes, the number of permits
  allowed, and the definition of the host.

  Discussion: Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER thanked the public for their comments,
  acknowledged that there was a place for STRs in Alhambra due to the lack of hotels, and
  stressed that there was a need for regulations to prevent bad actors. She discussed the City’s
  vision to expand affordable housing and discussed the overall total of STRs in Alhambra and
  the total capacity in overall permits with Director of Community Development HO. Ms.
  ANDRADE-STADLER supported the cap of 500 permits due to the fact that it was reasonable
  given the estimated total of existing STRs in the City and that it would help the City move
  towards the goal of creating more affordable housing opportunities. She suggested that
  perhaps they could “grandfather” in permits for some existing STR owners. Ms. ANDRADE-
  STADLER discussed the building inspection certification process with Mr. HO, discussed past
  police responses to STRs with Police Chief KENNEDY and City Manager BINNQUIST, and
  discussed responses to noise complaints with Chief KENNEDY.

  Councilmember MALONEY addressed public concerns regarding STR regulation over multi-
  family units and condominiums and discussed the proposed prohibition of STRs in multi-family
  complexes of more than five units with City Attorney MONTES and Mr. HO. Mr. MALONEY
  suggested that rather than focusing on condominiums, that the focus of the ordinance should
  be to regulate multi-family apartment sites in an effort to retain potential affordable rental units.
  He also supported a cap of 500 permits. Mr. MALONEY and Mr. HO discussed the revocation
  of permit due to 3 violations within a calendar year, the ability of residents to monitor and report
  STR properties within their neighborhood, STR compliance with Alhambra Municipal Building
  Codes, and imposing a fee for inspection of STRs or providing a list of outside inspectors for
  STR owners to conduct their own certified inspection. Mr. MALONEY requested further
  discussion of multi-family unit inspections during a Strategic Planning Session. Mr. MALONEY
  addressed comments regarding the definition of “host,” and expressed preference to keep the
  definition on an individual basis rather than companies with multiple properties. He reiterated
  Ms. Andrade-Stadler’s comments regarding the lack of hotels in Alhambra and the demand
  for STRs.

  Councilmember MAZA spoke to some of the benefits of STR services like AirBnB, the ability
  of Council to draft an ordinance which could be modified over time as new needs arise, and
  the needs of tourists visiting the City. Mr. MAZA and Mr. HO discussed the lack of fees
  collected by AirBnB revenue for the City. Mr. MAZA clarified his previous intention regarding
  the prohibition of permits for multi-family complexes and stated that condominium complexes
  would be exempt and that permits would be prohibited in multi-family apartment complexes of
  more than 5 units. He also addressed the definition of “host” in the ordinance, clarifying that
  4
9-23-24
   the intention was to limit corporate entities converting viable rental units into STR units. He
  discussed the definition of “host” as it would affect property management companies
  contracting with natural owners. He also discussed the cap on permits, and suggested that he
  would consider a higher number to accommodate existing operators. He echoed Mr. Maloney’s
  comments regarding certified building inspectors and the need for independent third-party
  inspectors to avoid properties being non-compliant with the Alhambra Municipal Code.

  Mayor PÉREZ acknowledged speakers as responsible owners and operators but also
  acknowledged illegal cases which used STRs for operations. She emphasized the need for
  regulation to provide safety and high quality of life for the community as well as addressing the
  housing crisis. She suggested that any current owners or operators prior to the ordinance
  would be allowed to keep their permits, and that the cap would be set after the existing permits
  could be accommodated. She agreed with Mr. Maloney’s comments regarding certified
  inspectors. She emphasized the need for monitoring repeated violations and discussed the
  process with Mr. HO and Mr. MONTES. She also discussed parking requirements with Mr.
  HO.

  Mr. MONTES addressed the discussion of setting a cap to permits allowed, and suggested
  that the ordinance could be modified to say that “the City would only issue up to a maximum
  of 500 active permits in any given time or such other cap as set by Council Resolution.” This
  would allow flexibility for Council to change the number of permits when a more accurate count
  could be calculated for existing permits. Mr. MONTES also acknowledged the definition of host
  which would eliminate several discussed concerns regarding existing operators and clarified
  that should the City undertake the task of inspecting STRs then appropriate staffing changes
  would have to be made in a short amount of time. Mr. MALONEY, Mr. MONTES, and Mr. HO
  discussed the concerns regarding third party inspections and Mr. HO clarified that some
  requirements could be addressed in the application process. Mr. MAZA and Mr. HO
  acknowledged that the ordinance as written could be further adapted as needs arise. Mr.
  MALONEY motioned to approve the ordinance with additional language suggested by Mr.
  MONTES regarding the cap on permits. The motion was seconded by Ms. ANDRADE-
  STADLER.

  Action Taken: City Council declared introduced for its first reading the following ordinance
entitled:

  Ordinance No. O2M24-4836: An Ordinance of the Alhambra City Council
  adding Chapter 5.92 – Short Term Rentals - to the Alhambra Municipal
  Code to protect public health, safety, and welfare by ensuring that the
  characteristics of residential neighborhoods are preserved

  which ordinance shall return for a second reading and adoption at the next Council
  meeting on October 14, 2024.

  Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, MALONEY, PÉREZ
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  LEE

5.  ACCEPT CALIFORNIA LIBRARY SERVICES ACT (CLSA) DISTRIBUTED FUNDS FROM
  THE SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA LIBRARY COOPERATIVE (SCLC) FOR ELECTRONIC
  RESOURCES AND APPROPRIATE FUNDS – F2M24-17, M2M24-169

  During the May 29, 204 meeting of SCLC, the administrative council voted to approve
  $365,773 in CLSA roll over funds to be allocated as one-time distribution to SCLC member
  5
9-23-24
   libraries to use on electronic resources. Based on a population-based formula, Alhambra’s
  distribution was $6,428. These funds would be utilized to the Overdrive/Libby platform to
  purchase e-books and e-audiobooks for the Library’s digital collection and was intended for
  public use. The funds would be expended in FY 2024-2025.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council accepted $6,428 from the Southern California Library
  Cooperative for the California Library Services Act fund distribution; appropriated revenue and
  expenditure funds in the amount of $6,428; and, directed staff to undertake the steps
  necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M24-169)

  Vote:  Moved:  MAZA  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  MALONEY, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  LEE

6.  ACCEPT GRANT: OFFICE OF TRAFFIC SAFETY (OTS) – SELECTIVE TRAFFIC
  ENFORCEMENT PROGRAM – F2M24-18, M2M24-170

  Staff requested that the City Council authorize staff to accept the Office of Traffic Safety grant
  in the amount of $148,000. The goal of the Office of Traffic Safety was to reduce the number
  of individuals killed or injured in crashes involving alcohol or other primary collision factors
  through grant funding for local law enforcement agencies. The Alhambra Police Department
  intended to utilize the funding for the FY 2024-2025 Selective Traffic Enforcement Program to
  enhance community safety through various enforcement and education programs. Such
  programs and services would include: DUI enforcement, awareness and education programs;
  bicycle and pedestrian safety enforcement and education; participation in programs such as
  National Walk to School Day, National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Winter & Summer
  Mobilizations, National Bicycle Safety Month, National Teen Driver Safety Week, National
  Distracted Driving Awareness Month, National Motorcycle Safety Month, National Child
  Passenger Safety Week, and California’s Pedestrian Safety Month.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council accepted the Office of Traffic Safety Grant in the amount
  of $148,000.00; authorize the Chief of Police to enter into a contract with the Office of Traffic
  Safety for grant implementation; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize
  Council’s action. (M2M24-170)

  Vote:  Moved:  MAZA  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  MALONEY, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  LEE

7.  RESOLUTION EXTENDING THE CITY OF ALHAMBRA’S OFFICIAL WELCOME AND
  GREETINGS TO THE HONORABLE SHINICHI NAKASHIGE, MAYOR, AND
  MUNICIPAL GOVERNMENT DELEGATION OF KIRISHIMA CITY – SISTER CITY TO
THE CITY OF ALHAMBRA – F2M7-80, R2M24-43

  In 2007, at the initiative of former Councilmember Gary Yamauchi, the City of Alhambra
  established a Sister City relationship between the City of Alhambra and Kirishima City, Japan.
  At the July 22, 2024 City Council meeting, Councilmember Maloney requested the Council’s
  6
9-23-24
   support to bring forward a resolution to officially welcome current Mayor of Kirishima City, the
  Honorable Shinichi Nakashige, and the Municipal Government Delegation from Kirishima City
  who would be visiting the City of Alhambra on October 25, 2024. This resolution was intended
  to extend the City’s official welcome and greetings to the delegation from Kirishima City.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M24-43 entitled: A Resolution
  of the Alhambra City Council extending the City of Alhambra’s Official Welcome and Greetings
  to the Honorable Shinichi Nakashige, Mayor, and Municipal Government Delegation of
  Kirishima City – Sister City to the City of Alhambra

  Vote:  Moved:  MAZA  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  MALONEY, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  LEE

8.  AMENDED PLAN FOR USE OF AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN ACT OF 2021 (ARPA) RELIEF
  FUNDS – F2M21-67, M2M24-171

  On January 24, 2022, January 17, 2023, July 24, 2023, and June 24, 2024, the City Council
  amended the ARPA Plan to allocate funds for various critical needs. This included addressing
  deferred maintenance for City buildings and facilities; replacing aging City equipment; and
  modernizing technology systems. City staff were currently managing the City’s ARPA projects,
  utilizing cost savings, closing inactive projects, and seeking alternative funding for any price
  escalations. As the Treasury’s deadline of December 31, 2024 approaches for encumbering
  ARPA funds, staff reviewed the ARPA project listings and closed all inactive projects. Staff
  recommended reallocating $129,740 in unspent funds to the Dog Park project, increasing its
  total allocation to $729,740. This action would ensure that the funds were utilized effectively
  and prevent any potential return to the federal government. Staff further requested the Council
  direct the Finance Director to make the necessary budget adjustments for all approved ARPA
  funds and utilize savings from completed ARPA projects to offset any overages from current
  or backup projects.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved the amended American Rescue Plan Funds
  (ARPA) plan as outlined in the Director of Finance’s September 23, 2024 report; authorize the
  Finance Director to amend the ARPA budget for all approved ARPA funds and utilize savings
  to offset overages within current or backup ARPA projects; and, directed staff to undertake
  the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s action. (M2M24-171)

  Vote:  Moved:  MAZA  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  MALONEY, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  LEE

9.  FY 2023-2024 TO FY 2024-2025 CARRYOVERS - F2M23-17, F2M24-17, R2M24-42

  Staff requested that the City Council adopt a resolution approving certain fiscal year-end
  carryovers from fiscal year 2023-2024 to fiscal year 2024-2025 and the reappropriation of
  outstanding encumbrances at the close of the fiscal year 2023-2024.

  7
9-23-24
   Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  Council adopted Resolution No. R2M24-42 entitled: A Resolution of
  the Alhambra City Council approving those certain fiscal year-end carryovers from fiscal year
  2023/24 to fiscal year 2024/25 and reappropriation of outstanding encumbrances at the close
  of the fiscal year 2023/24

  Vote:  Moved:  MAZA  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  MALONEY, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  LEE

10.  AUTHORIZE RFP: PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING DESIGN SERVICES FOR THE
  WATER MAIN REPLACEMENT PROJECT ON CONCORD AVENUE, LA PALOMA
  AVENUE AND MERIDIAN AVENUE – F2M24-63, RFP2M24-22

  The Utilities Department regularly installs water mains to replace aging pipelines and to
  improve system reliability and water quality. The four-inch cast iron water main pipes on La
  Paloma Avenue between Main Street and Concord Avenue and on Meridian Avenue between
  Main Street and Concord Avenue were installed in 1922. The six-inch cast iron water main
  pipe on Concord Avenue between Orange Grove Avenue and La Paloma Avenue was installed
  in 1923.The water main pipes had a history of breaks. These water main lines should be
  replaced and would greatly improve flow and firefighting capabilities in an emergency. This
  project replaced the existing four-inch and six-inch cast iron water mains with new 8-inch
  ductile iron water mains.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved the distribution of a Request for Proposals for
  Professional Engineering Design Services for the Water Main Replacement Project on
  Concord Avenue, La Paloma Avenue, and Meridian Avenue with proposals due no later than
  4:00 p.m. on Thursday, October 24, 2024; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary
  to finalize the Council’s action.

  Vote:  Moved:  MAZA  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  MALONEY, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  LEE

11.  REJECT BIDS RECEIVED AND AUTHORIZE A NEW NOTICE INVITING BIDS FOR
THE DESIGN AND PURCHASE OF ALHAMBRA PLACEMAKING SIGNAGE – F2M24-  51,
N2M24-89, N2M24-117, M2M24-172

  On July 22, 2024, the City Council approved the circulation of a Notice Inviting Bids for the
  Design and Purchase of Alhambra Placemaking Signage. On August 15, 2024, the City Clerk
  opened the two bids received. The lowest bid did not demonstrate that it would provide contract
  work that amounted to at least 51 percent of the contract price. The second bid far exceeded
  the project budget. Therefore, staff recommended rejecting both bids received for this project.
  Specifications and bid documentation for the Design and Purchase of Alhambra Placemaking
  Signage would be recirculated and made available on the City’s website and at the Office of
  the City Clerk. Bids will be due no later than 10:30 a.m. on November 7, 2024 in the office of
  the City Clerk and will be publicly opened at 11:00 a.m. that same day.

  8
9-23-24
   Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council rejected the bids received in response to Notice Inviting
  Bids N2M24-89 for the Design and Purchase of Alhambra Placemaking Signage; authorized
  a new Notice Inviting Bids for the Design and Purchase of Alhambra Placemaking Signage
  (N2M24-117); and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s
  action. (M2M24-172)

  Vote:  Moved:  MAZA  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  MALONEY, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  LEE

12. CONTRACT AMENDMENT: ARCHITECTURAL SERVICES FOR THE ALHAMBRA
COMMUNITY CENTER – F2M22-65, C2M23-66, M2M24-173

  On July 24, 2023, the City Council authorized an agreement with KFA LLP to provide
  professional architecture services for the design and development of the Alhambra Community
  Center. KFA’s original scope of work included the demolition of the existing Shorb Street
  Medical Clinic building and the construction of an entirely new 25,000 square foot Alhambra
  Community Center building. The contract was amended on July 22, 2024 to address tasks
  that were not associated with the original scope of work. A second amendment was needed
  for scope changes that require the design of the 9,000 square foot adaptive reuse building
  and the design of three different sized community centers. The designs included a 17,000
  square foot building to complete construction documents and development designs to expand
  the building to 21,000 and 25,000 square feet. The 9,000 square foot adaptative reuse
  introduced analysis and complexity that required specialized design approaches distinct from
  those required for a new construction building. No additional budget was necessary to fund
  the additional services. Accordingly, this amendment requested an additional $258,210 which
  resulted in a new total contract not to exceed $1,867,835.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved a contract amendment, subject to final language
  approval by the City Manager and City Attorney, by and between the City of Alhambra and
  KFA LLP., for professional architecture services associated with the redesign of the Alhambra
  Community Center to add a not to exceed sum of $258,210 to KFA’s current contract; and,
  directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s action. (M2M24-173)

  Vote:  Moved:  MAZA  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  MALONEY, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  LEE

13.  AUTHORIZE RFP: PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION
SERVICES FOR THE SEWER MAIN REPLACEMENT PROJECT ON GLENAVEN AVENUE,
ORANGE GROVE AVENUE, MIDWICK DRIVE, LA GOLONDRINA AVENUE  AND  ROSS
AVENUE – F2M24-64, RFP2M24-23

  The Sewer Master Plan identified the Sewer Replacement Project on Glenaven Avenue (from
  Glen View Dr. to Orange Grove Ave.), Orange Grove Avenue (from Glenaven Ave. to Midwick
  Dr.), Midwick Drive (from Orange Grove Ave. to West of Ramona Terrace), and at La
  Golondrina Avenue, and Ross Avenue as deficient in capacity. The existing 12-inch pipe was
  9
9-23-24
   expected to be surcharged during existing and ultimate peak wet weather conditions. A portion
  would be surcharged during existing and ultimate peak dry weather conditions. The Master
  Plan recommended replacement of the existing sewer main with a larger diameter sewer main.
  As part of the City of Alhambra’s ongoing Capital Improvement Program, this project would
  provide engineering design, plans, and preparation of bid specifications for the replacement of
  approximately 2,525 feet of existing 12-inch sewer main with a larger capacity sewer main.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved the distribution of a Request for Proposals
  (RFP) for Professional Engineering Design and Construction Services for the Sewer
